claims.title: Dalmatia and Pannonia become Roman provinces
claims.summary: After the crushing of the great Illyrian (Pannonian) revolt, Rome organised the eastern Adriatic and its hinterland into the provinces of Dalmatia and Pannonia, beginning centuries of Roman rule and urban life along the coast.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Croatia: From Roman Dalmatia to the Adriatic republic, a nation forged between empires, partitioned and reborn through war.", terralore.co/country/HRV/chronicle#ev-9-dalmatia-and-pannonia-become-roman-provinces, claim TL:HRV:event:9:dalmatia-and-pannonia-become-roman-provinces, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Diocletian's Palace at Split
claims.summary: The Dalmatian-born emperor Diocletian built an immense fortified palace near Salona around the turn of the fourth century; the historic core of Split later grew within its walls, today the most complete surviving Roman palace.

sources.label: Historical Complex of Split with the Palace of Diocletian

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Croatia: From Roman Dalmatia to the Adriatic republic, a nation forged between empires, partitioned and reborn through war.", terralore.co/country/HRV/chronicle#ev-305-diocletian-s-palace-at-split, claim TL:HRV:event:305:diocletian-s-palace-at-split, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Slavic settlement and the coming of the Croats
claims.summary: Avar and Slavic invasions destroyed the Roman provincial order, including the capital Salona; the Croats settled the former provinces of Dalmatia and Pannonia and gradually organised duchies of their own.

sources.label: Croatia in Europe through the Ages: Development of the State

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Croatia: From Roman Dalmatia to the Adriatic republic, a nation forged between empires, partitioned and reborn through war.", terralore.co/country/HRV/chronicle#ev-626-slavic-settlement-and-the-coming-of-the-croats, claim TL:HRV:event:626:slavic-settlement-and-the-coming-of-the-croats, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Papal recognition of Duke Branimir
claims.summary: Pope John VIII acknowledged the rule of Duke Branimir over the Croatian realm, aligning the Croats with the Latin Church of Rome and marking the emergence of Croatia as a recognised state.

sources.label: Croatia in Europe through the Ages: Development of the State

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Croatia: From Roman Dalmatia to the Adriatic republic, a nation forged between empires, partitioned and reborn through war.", terralore.co/country/HRV/chronicle#ev-879-papal-recognition-of-duke-branimir, claim TL:HRV:event:879:papal-recognition-of-duke-branimir, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Tomislav recognised as king of the Croats
claims.summary: Having united the Croats of Dalmatia and Pannonia and held off the Magyars and Bulgars, Tomislav was addressed as king in letters of Pope John X and is regarded by tradition as the first king of a unified Croatia.

sources.label: Croatia in Europe through the Ages: Development of the State

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Croatia: From Roman Dalmatia to the Adriatic republic, a nation forged between empires, partitioned and reborn through war.", terralore.co/country/HRV/chronicle#ev-925-tomislav-recognised-as-king-of-the-croats, claim TL:HRV:event:925:tomislav-recognised-as-king-of-the-croats, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Coronation of Demetrius Zvonimir
claims.summary: Zvonimir was crowned king of Croatia with the sanction of the papacy, the last of the great native rulers and a symbol of the medieval kingdom at its height.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Croatia: From Roman Dalmatia to the Adriatic republic, a nation forged between empires, partitioned and reborn through war.", terralore.co/country/HRV/chronicle#ev-1075-coronation-of-demetrius-zvonimir, claim TL:HRV:event:1075:coronation-of-demetrius-zvonimir, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Personal union with Hungary
claims.summary: King Coloman of Hungary was crowned king of Croatia and Dalmatia, joining the crowns in a personal union; Croatian tradition records the terms in the Pacta conventa, under which Croatia kept its Sabor and its ban.

sources.label: Croatia in Europe through the Ages: Development of the State

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Croatia: From Roman Dalmatia to the Adriatic republic, a nation forged between empires, partitioned and reborn through war.", terralore.co/country/HRV/chronicle#ev-1102-personal-union-with-hungary, claim TL:HRV:event:1102:personal-union-with-hungary, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Venice secures Dalmatia
claims.summary: After long rivalry Venice took control of most of the Dalmatian coast, which it would govern for nearly four centuries until 1797, shaping the art, architecture and administration of the coastal cities.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Croatia: From Roman Dalmatia to the Adriatic republic, a nation forged between empires, partitioned and reborn through war.", terralore.co/country/HRV/chronicle#ev-1420-venice-secures-dalmatia, claim TL:HRV:event:1420:venice-secures-dalmatia, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Republic of Ragusa (Dubrovnik)
claims.summary: Dubrovnik governed itself as an aristocratic merchant republic, paying tribute to the Ottoman sultan after 1458 while rivalling Venice in trade; its walled old city is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Croatia: From Roman Dalmatia to the Adriatic republic, a nation forged between empires, partitioned and reborn through war.", terralore.co/country/HRV/chronicle#ev-1458-the-republic-of-ragusa-dubrovnik, claim TL:HRV:event:1458:the-republic-of-ragusa-dubrovnik, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Dalmatian towns under Venice
claims.summary: Coastal cities such as Trogir flourished under Venetian rule, acquiring fine Romanesque, Renaissance and Baroque buildings; the historic island town of Trogir is preserved as a UNESCO World Heritage Site of the Venetian period.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Croatia: From Roman Dalmatia to the Adriatic republic, a nation forged between empires, partitioned and reborn through war.", terralore.co/country/HRV/chronicle#ev-1500-the-dalmatian-towns-under-venice, claim TL:HRV:event:1500:the-dalmatian-towns-under-venice, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Habsburgs elected to the Croatian throne
claims.summary: Facing Ottoman conquest after the disaster at Mohacs in 1526, the Croatian nobility elected the Habsburg Ferdinand I as king, binding Croatia's defence to the Austrian monarchy.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Croatia: From Roman Dalmatia to the Adriatic republic, a nation forged between empires, partitioned and reborn through war.", terralore.co/country/HRV/chronicle#ev-1527-habsburgs-elected-to-the-croatian-throne, claim TL:HRV:event:1527:habsburgs-elected-to-the-croatian-throne, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Military Frontier
claims.summary: To hold the line against the Ottomans the Habsburgs created the Military Frontier, a militarised border zone settled by free soldier-peasants, including many Serb and Vlach refugees, who served in exchange for land and privileges.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Croatia: From Roman Dalmatia to the Adriatic republic, a nation forged between empires, partitioned and reborn through war.", terralore.co/country/HRV/chronicle#ev-1578-the-military-frontier, claim TL:HRV:event:1578:the-military-frontier, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Great Dubrovnik earthquake
claims.summary: A devastating earthquake struck Dubrovnik in 1667, destroying much of the city, killing thousands and ending the long prosperity of the Ragusan republic.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Croatia: From Roman Dalmatia to the Adriatic republic, a nation forged between empires, partitioned and reborn through war.", terralore.co/country/HRV/chronicle#ev-1667-the-great-dubrovnik-earthquake, claim TL:HRV:event:1667:the-great-dubrovnik-earthquake, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Napoleon's Illyrian Provinces
claims.summary: Napoleon gathered much of the coast and hinterland into the short-lived Illyrian Provinces, an episode that helped stir a sense of shared South Slav identity among the Croats.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Croatia: From Roman Dalmatia to the Adriatic republic, a nation forged between empires, partitioned and reborn through war.", terralore.co/country/HRV/chronicle#ev-1809-napoleon-s-illyrian-provinces, claim TL:HRV:event:1809:napoleon-s-illyrian-provinces, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Illyrian movement and national revival
claims.summary: Led by Ljudevit Gaj, intellectuals and clergy promoted a standard Croatian literary language and South Slav cultural unity, laying the foundations of the modern Croatian nation.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Croatia: From Roman Dalmatia to the Adriatic republic, a nation forged between empires, partitioned and reborn through war.", terralore.co/country/HRV/chronicle#ev-1835-the-illyrian-movement-and-national-revival, claim TL:HRV:event:1835:the-illyrian-movement-and-national-revival, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Croatian made the official language
claims.summary: The Croatian Sabor adopted Croatian in place of Latin as the official language, a milestone of the national revival and a response to the imposition of Hungarian.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Croatia: From Roman Dalmatia to the Adriatic republic, a nation forged between empires, partitioned and reborn through war.", terralore.co/country/HRV/chronicle#ev-1847-croatian-made-the-official-language, claim TL:HRV:event:1847:croatian-made-the-official-language, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Croatian-Hungarian Settlement (Nagodba)
claims.summary: Within the Dual Monarchy created in 1867, the Nagodba granted Croatia-Slavonia limited autonomy under its own ban and Sabor, though real authority remained with Budapest.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Croatia: From Roman Dalmatia to the Adriatic republic, a nation forged between empires, partitioned and reborn through war.", terralore.co/country/HRV/chronicle#ev-1868-the-croatian-hungarian-settlement-nagodba, claim TL:HRV:event:1868:the-croatian-hungarian-settlement-nagodba, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Entry into the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes
claims.summary: After the collapse of Austria-Hungary, the Croatian lands joined Serbia and Montenegro in the new South Slav kingdom proclaimed on 1 December 1918, later renamed Yugoslavia.

sources.label: Kingdom of Serbs, Croats, and Slovenes

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Croatia: From Roman Dalmatia to the Adriatic republic, a nation forged between empires, partitioned and reborn through war.", terralore.co/country/HRV/chronicle#ev-1918-entry-into-the-kingdom-of-serbs-croats-and, claim TL:HRV:event:1918:entry-into-the-kingdom-of-serbs-croats-and, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Independent State of Croatia (NDH)
claims.summary: Following the Axis invasion, Germany and Italy set up the Independent State of Croatia, a puppet state run by the fascist Ustase under Ante Pavelic, embracing Croatia and Bosnia and Herzegovina.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Croatia: From Roman Dalmatia to the Adriatic republic, a nation forged between empires, partitioned and reborn through war.", terralore.co/country/HRV/chronicle#ev-1941-the-independent-state-of-croatia-ndh, claim TL:HRV:event:1941:the-independent-state-of-croatia-ndh, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Jasenovac camp
claims.summary: The Ustase regime operated its largest camp complex at Jasenovac, where it murdered an estimated 77,000 to 99,000 people, among them tens of thousands of Serbs, Jews and Roma, between 1941 and 1945.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Croatia: From Roman Dalmatia to the Adriatic republic, a nation forged between empires, partitioned and reborn through war.", terralore.co/country/HRV/chronicle#ev-1941-the-jasenovac-camp, claim TL:HRV:event:1941:the-jasenovac-camp, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Croatia in socialist Yugoslavia
claims.summary: The Partisan victory under Tito made Croatia one of the six republics of a federal socialist Yugoslavia, ending the Ustase state and beginning four decades of communist rule.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Croatia: From Roman Dalmatia to the Adriatic republic, a nation forged between empires, partitioned and reborn through war.", terralore.co/country/HRV/chronicle#ev-1945-croatia-in-socialist-yugoslavia, claim TL:HRV:event:1945:croatia-in-socialist-yugoslavia, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Croatian Spring
claims.summary: Reformers and students in the 'Croatian Spring' demanded greater economic and constitutional autonomy; Tito crushed the movement and purged its leaders, though the 1974 constitution later widened republican rights.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Croatia: From Roman Dalmatia to the Adriatic republic, a nation forged between empires, partitioned and reborn through war.", terralore.co/country/HRV/chronicle#ev-1971-the-croatian-spring, claim TL:HRV:event:1971:the-croatian-spring, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Declaration of independence
claims.summary: The Croatian Sabor declared independence from Yugoslavia on 25 June 1991; rebel Serbs backed by the Yugoslav army seized nearly a third of the country and proclaimed the Republic of Serbian Krajina, igniting war.

sources.label: The Conflicts (former Yugoslavia)
sources.publisher: International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Croatia: From Roman Dalmatia to the Adriatic republic, a nation forged between empires, partitioned and reborn through war.", terralore.co/country/HRV/chronicle#ev-1991-declaration-of-independence, claim TL:HRV:event:1991:declaration-of-independence, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The fall of Vukovar
claims.summary: After a siege of some three months, Vukovar fell to the Yugoslav army and Serb forces on 18 November 1991; two days later 194 people taken from the hospital were killed at the Ovcara farm, a crime later prosecuted at the ICTY.

sources.label: Vukovar Crimes
sources.publisher: International Residual Mechanism for Criminal Tribunals (UN)

sources.label: The Conflicts (former Yugoslavia)
sources.publisher: International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia

claims.title: International recognition
claims.summary: Croatia won international recognition as a sovereign state in 1992; the United States recognised it on 7 April 1992, and the country was admitted to the United Nations.

sources.label: A Guide to U.S. History of Recognition, Diplomatic, and Consular Relations: Croatia
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

sources.label: The Conflicts (former Yugoslavia)
sources.publisher: International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Croatia: From Roman Dalmatia to the Adriatic republic, a nation forged between empires, partitioned and reborn through war.", terralore.co/country/HRV/chronicle#ev-1992-international-recognition, claim TL:HRV:event:1992:international-recognition, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Operation Storm
claims.summary: In August 1995 the Croatian army launched Operation Storm, which within days overran the Republic of Serbian Krajina and ended its existence, accompanied by the flight of tens of thousands of Serbs; generals later tried at the ICTY were acquitted on appeal in 2012.

sources.label: The Conflicts (former Yugoslavia)
sources.publisher: International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia

sources.label: ICTY Weekly Press Briefing, 21 November 2012 (Gotovina and Markac appeals judgement)
sources.publisher: International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia

claims.title: Piran Bay arbitration award
claims.summary: The Permanent Court of Arbitration issued its Final Award on the Croatia-Slovenia border in the Gulf of Piran; Croatia, which had withdrawn from the process in 2015, declared it did not consider itself bound by the ruling.

sources.label: Arbitration (Croatia-Slovenia border, Final Award 29 June 2017)
sources.publisher: Government of the Republic of Slovenia (gov.si)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Croatia: From Roman Dalmatia to the Adriatic republic, a nation forged between empires, partitioned and reborn through war.", terralore.co/country/HRV/chronicle#ev-2017-piran-bay-arbitration-award, claim TL:HRV:event:2017:piran-bay-arbitration-award, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Plitvice Lakes inscribed by UNESCO
claims.summary: Plitvice Lakes, Croatia's oldest national park, was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1979 for the ongoing formation of tufa barriers that dam its waters into a chain of lakes and waterfalls, the country's first World Heritage site.

sources.label: Plitvice Lakes National Park — 45 years on the UNESCO World Heritage List
sources.publisher: Plitvice Lakes National Park (Republic of Croatia)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Croatia: From Roman Dalmatia to the Adriatic republic, a nation forged between empires, partitioned and reborn through war.", terralore.co/country/HRV/chronicle#ev-1979-plitvice-lakes-inscribed-by-unesco, claim TL:HRV:event:1979:plitvice-lakes-inscribed-by-unesco, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Accession to the European Union
claims.summary: Croatia joined the European Union on 1 July 2013 as its 28th member, after a 2012 referendum, having joined NATO in 2009; it adopted the euro and entered the Schengen area on 1 January 2023.

sources.label: On 1 July 2013 Croatia has become the 28th Member State of the European Union
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs of the Republic of Croatia

sources.label: Croatia — Enlargement (Member State as of 1 July 2013)
sources.publisher: European Commission, Enlargement and Eastern Neighbourhood
